newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX opts for breather, banks shares fall.
newsitem.headline: German DAX opts for breather, banks shares fall.

text.p: German shares took the chance to consolidate on Thursday, dropping sharply as investors took profits on banking stocks after days of an apparently inexorable rally.
The 30-share DAX index ended a volatile bourse session down 70.35 points, or 1.6 percent, at 4,335.74 points.

Bank shares were the outright losers, with Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, which had surged some 40 percent this week, dropping nearly 11 percent to 102.50 marks after reporting six-month profit that was slightly below forecasts.
The HDAX bank share index, which monitors a broad spectrum of banking shares in the top 100 German stocks, fell nearly five percent.
Dealers said the consolidation was welcome relief after a frantic few days.
"It wouldn't hurt to get right back down near 4,000 (DAX points)," said one dealer.
Hypo-Bank banking analyst Christine Winkler downplayed the drop in banking shares. "It's been crazy recently," she said. "Bank share prices have totally decoupled from fundamentals."
Commerzbank shares fell five percent to 62 marks.
Commerzbank reported that its first-half operating profit after provisions rose 23.2 percent to 1.63 billion marks, which was above analysts' expectations.

Bayerische Vereinsbank, which accelerated the bank share frenzy earlier this week when it revealed plans to merge with Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel Bank, saw its operating profit after provisions rise 15.2 percent to 765.7 million.

Support for the market came from the ever-firmer dollar and a higher, if unspectacularly so, close on Wall Street. The Bundesbank's decision to leave interest rates unchanged was expected and had minimal impact.

"This market is like a train moving full-steam ahead, which means it is going to take a while for it to slow down. We could lose of couple of hundred points and it would not make any difference," a Frankfurt trader said.
As to whether or not the market is getting ready for a crash, dealers said that there was too much caution around.

"The word "crash" is on everyone's lips and people are saying the market is overheating. But look at the backdrop to this bull run -- low interest rates, weak mark -- and it's hard to see any evidence pointing to a real crash," he said.
